quests.conceptTitle: Modifier Placement: Dangling Modifier Avoidance (Introductory -ing Phrase)
quests.targetSentence: Walking through the park, she noticed the cherry blossoms had bloomed.
quests.awkwardSentence: Walking through the park, walking through the park she noticed the cherry blossoms had bloomed.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Walking through the park' describes 'she', the subject right after the comma. If the sentence instead began with something else there, the phrase would dangle, with no clear person doing the walking.
quests.nativeTip: Ask yourself who is doing the walking, then place this phrase right before that person, at the very start of the sentence.
quests.visualAnchor: 🎯 Place 'Walking through the park,' right next to the word it describes: 'Walking through the park, she noticed the cherry blossoms had bloomed.'
quests.comedyNote: Misplacing 'Walking through the park,' produces awkward phrasing like: 'Walking through the park, walking through the park she noticed the cherry blossoms had bloomed.'. Always anchor modifiers adjacent to the words they modify.
